games.title: Risk of Rain
games.dev: Hopoo Games (Duncan Drummond and Paul Morse)
games.note: Made by two University of Washington students; the longer a run lasts, the harder it gets.

games.title: Risk of Rain 2
games.note: Early access began in March 2019; the full release followed in August 2020.

games.title: Megabonk
games.note: Its anonymous solo developer moved launch day to avoid Hollow Knight: Silksong; it sold a million copies in two weeks.

games.title: Darkest Dungeon
games.dev: Red Hook Studios (Chris Bourassa and Tyler Sigman)
games.note: Its stress system drew on a Band of Brothers episode about a soldier who can no longer keep fighting.

games.title: The Bard's Tale
games.note: A party-based dungeon crawl beneath the town of Skara Brae.

games.title: Enter the Gungeon
games.note: Four developers left Mythic Entertainment in 2014 to found Dodge Roll and make it.

games.title: Ikaruga
games.note: Switching the ship between black and white lets it absorb bullets of the same color.

games.title: Nuclear Throne
games.dev: Vlambeer (Jan Willem Nijman and Rami Ismail)
games.note: Began as Wasteland Kings, made in a 48-hour Mojam game jam in 2013.

games.title: Crypt of the NecroDancer
games.note: Every move must land on the beat of Danny Baranowsky's soundtrack, and it can be played on a dance pad.

games.title: Cadence of Hyrule
games.note: Grew out of Brace Yourself Games asking Nintendo about a Zelda-themed add-on for NecroDancer.

games.title: Dead Cells
games.note: Motion Twin first planned a co-op tower defense follow-up to its browser game Die2Nite.

games.title: Windblown
games.note: Motion Twin's follow-up to Dead Cells; in early access since October 2024, with a full release planned for 2026.

games.title: Bastion
games.note: A narrator reacts to everything the player does; most of the team built it in a house in San Jose.

games.title: Pyre
games.note: An attempt at a branching, open-ended story; few players replayed it, which pushed Supergiant toward a roguelike for Hades.

games.title: Returnal
games.note: Directed by Harry Krueger; released on PlayStation 5 in April 2021 and on PC in 2023.

games.title: Nex Machina
games.note: Housemarque made it together with Robotron co-creator Eugene Jarvis.

games.title: Loop Hero
games.note: Grew from a 2019 Ludum Dare jam game in which a hero walks a loop while the player builds around it.

games.title: Noita
games.note: Every pixel is physically simulated, so liquids flow, fire spreads and walls crumble.

games.title: Liero
games.note: Finnish freeware duels between armed worms in destructible caves.

games.title: Cult of the Lamb
games.note: The studio turned to occult horror after feeling its earlier cute games were seen as being for children.

games.title: Don't Starve
games.note: Its dark, cartoonish art drew on Tim Burton and Edward Gorey.

links.took: Rogue popularized runs with permanent death and randomly found items.
links.added: Side-scrolling co-op action where the difficulty climbs with every minute you survive.

links.took: Survivors, stacking items and a timer that raises the difficulty.
links.added: A move into 3D third-person shooting for up to four online players.

links.took: 3D run-based action where stacking items make you absurdly strong.
links.added: Survivors-style automatic attacks across open 3D maps.
links.extra: A GamesRadar+ headline reported it being hailed as a mix of Vampire Survivors and Risk of Rain 2.

links.took: Automatic attacks, swarms of enemies and level-up upgrade choices.
links.added: Full 3D terrain with jumping and verticality.

links.took: A party lined up in ranks, where position decides who can attack.
links.added: Stress and afflictions that make heroes crack under the horror.

src.t: Wikipedia: Darkest Dungeon, citing Rock Paper Shotgun, 2017

links.extra: Chris Bourassa and Tyler Sigman loved old crawlers like The Bard's Tale but felt they lacked a human element.

links.took: Rogue popularized randomized dungeons and permanent death.
links.added: Losing heroes for good from a roster you manage between expeditions.

links.took: Stress, afflictions, rank-based turn-based combat and gothic art.
links.added: A stagecoach road trip and relationships between party members.

links.took: Room-by-room roguelike floors and a big item pool; one of its biggest influences.
links.added: Hundreds of joke guns, bullet-hell patterns and a dodge roll.

src.t: Dave Crooks (Dodge Roll), Q&A, Game Developer (Gamasutra), 2016

links.extra: Lead designer Dave Crooks also named Nuclear Throne, Spelunky, Dark Souls and Metal Gear Solid as influences.

links.took: Fast, punchy top-down roguelike shooting.
links.added: Dodge rolls, tables to flip for cover, and bullet-pun humor.

src.t: Dave Crooks (Dodge Roll), Q&A, Game Developer (Gamasutra), 2016

links.took: Rolling through attacks to avoid them.
links.added: The same escape applied to dense bullet patterns in a twin-stick shooter.

src.t: Wikipedia: Enter the Gungeon, citing Game Developer, 2016

links.took: A mechanic for dodging many bullets at once.
links.added: Reworked as a dodge roll with brief invulnerability.

src.t: Wikipedia: Enter the Gungeon, citing Game Developer, 2016

links.took: Active reload: timing a reload for a bonus.
links.added: Kept only as a power-up item rather than a core mechanic.

src.t: Wikipedia: Enter the Gungeon, citing Game Developer, 2016

links.took: Vlambeer's punchy guns, screen shake and instant restarts.
links.added: Procedural wasteland levels, mutations and characters with unique powers.

links.took: Rogue popularized randomized levels with permanent death.
links.added: All of it played at arcade speed as a top-down shooter.

links.took: A hard game you can still master, where every death feels like your own fault.
links.added: Every move must land on the beat of the music.

src.t: Wikipedia: Crypt of the NecroDancer, citing Ryan Clark in Mashable

links.took: Rogue popularized grid-based, turn-based dungeon crawling with permadeath.
links.added: Turns tick with the music, leaving no time to stop and think.

links.took: Brace Yourself Games' beat-based movement and combat.
links.added: Hyrule, with Link and Zelda as heroes and remixed Zelda music.

links.took: Hyrule's overworld, characters, items and music.
links.added: Everything moves to the beat, under NecroDancer's rhythm rules.

links.took: Item-driven gameplay, which producer Steve Filby called a significant influence.
links.added: Fluid 2D melee combat in a castle whose layout changes every run.

links.took: The Engineer's turrets and buildable gadgets.
links.added: Turrets and traps as skills, paired with two weapons.

links.took: Metroidvania exploration through an interconnected castle.
links.added: A layout that reshuffles each run, giving rise to the label roguevania.

links.took: Punishing but readable melee; reviewers compared the combat to Dark Souls.
links.added: Faster 2D action where death sends you back to the start.

src.t: Wikipedia: Dead Cells, citing Rock Paper Shotgun, 2017

links.took: What Motion Twin learned making Dead Cells' combat and runs.
links.added: 3D co-op action for up to three players.

links.took: Metagame ideas the team tried out, borrowed from Hades.
links.added: Fast, dash-heavy 3D combat built for online co-op.

links.took: Metagame ideas the team tried out, borrowed from The Binding of Isaac.
links.added: Fast 3D combat built around online co-op.

links.took: Founders Amir Rao and Gavin Simon, who worked at EA on Command & Conquer 3.
links.added: A small action RPG with a narrator who reacts to everything you do.

links.took: Supergiant's team, Jen Zee's art, Darren Korb's music and narration as a core device.
links.added: A talking sword, and pausing time to plan combos of combined abilities.

links.took: Supergiant's illustrated look, Darren Korb's music and story-first design.
links.added: A party-based journey with mystical ball-game rites, where losing never ends the story.

links.took: Branching storytelling from Pyre, which the team felt suited a roguelike better.
links.added: Fast isometric combat and a story that advances with every death.

src.t: Wikipedia: Hades, citing Rock Paper Shotgun (2020) and Gamasutra (2019)
TheGamer, How Hades was built on Pyre

links.extra: Few players replayed Pyre, so Supergiant moved its branching narrative into a format built for replay.

links.took: A modern roguelike's run-by-run choices between upgrades.
links.added: Characters and story you return to after every run, plus Olympian boons.
links.extra: VICE's Patrick Klepek, writing after interviewing Greg Kasavin, named Slay the Spire and Dead Cells as inspirations.

links.took: Fast, fluid action married to roguelike runs.
links.added: A narrative that moves forward with each death.

links.took: Housemarque's dense bullet patterns and twitchy arcade shooting.
links.added: A third-person roguelike on a shifting alien planet, with a psychological story.

links.took: Eugene Jarvis, Robotron's co-creator, and its twin-stick, rescue-the-humans arena shooting.
links.added: Voxel explosions and Housemarque's score-chasing design.

links.took: Rogue popularized runs that reset with newly randomized levels.
links.added: A big-budget third-person shooter with a time loop explaining each restart.

links.took: Housemarque's third-person bullet-hell shooting from Returnal.
links.added: A new hero and a new world, the planet Carcosa.

links.took: Rogue popularized runs with permanent death and random loot.
links.added: A hero who walks a loop alone while you place cards that build the world.

links.took: Destructible terrain and chaotic weapons in side-view caves.
links.added: Every pixel simulated, spell-building wands and roguelike runs.

src.t: Wikipedia: Noita, citing Nolla Games' 2019 press release

links.took: Rogue popularized randomized levels and permanent death.
links.added: A physics-simulated world where fire, liquids and gases react to each other.

links.took: Rogue popularized randomized dungeon runs with permadeath.
links.added: Runs that supply a cult you build, with followers to feed, preach to and sacrifice.

links.took: Exploring a survival world with few instructions; one of the team's biggest influences.
links.added: A gothic Tim Burton-like look, hunger and sanity meters, and permanent death.

src.t: Wikipedia: Don't Starve, citing Kevin Forbes (Klei) in Gamasutra, 2012

links.took: Rogue popularized randomly generated worlds and permanent death.
links.added: Open-ended wilderness survival with crafting and a sanity meter.

links.took: Klei's wilderness survival, crafting, hunger and sanity.
links.added: Online co-op for up to six players.
